add_metrology_object_rectangle2_measure — MEASURE1D model op

• Data kinds: metrologymodel → scalar

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.add_metrology_object_rectangle2_measure(model, row, col, phi, l1, l2, n: 'int' = 40) -> 'int' (to call the implementation directly, import metrology; metrology.add_metrology_object_rectangle2_measure(model, row, col, phi, l1, l2, n: 'int' = 40) -> 'int'; from the registry, opsmeasure1d.get("add_metrology_object_rectangle2_measure"))

Usage

Adds a rectangle metrology object (add_metrology_object_rectangle2_measure). phi = orientation of the l1 side (from the col axis, in radians), l1/l2 = half side lengths.

Stacks the reference rectangle (centre (row, col) [px], half side length l1 in the phi direction, and half side length l2 in the orthogonal direction) onto model["objects"] (the dict is updated in place). apply_metrology_model places max(2, n // 4) points on each of the 4 sides at equal spacing, avoiding the corners, measures edges along the outward normal of each side, and with a rectangle fit recomputes the centre, orientation and half side lengths.

• phi: radians measured from the col axis (x) toward the row axis (image downward) (same convention as gen_measure_rectangle2).

• l1, l2: half side lengths [px] (not full lengths).

• n: guideline for the total number of samples (default 40 → 10 points per side). Even below 4, 2 points per side are placed.

• Arguments are not validated. The return value is the index of the added position (starting at 0).

• params of the apply result is row / col / phi / l1 / l2, and after refitting they are reordered so that l1 >= l2 (the long side is l1) -- even if the reference gives l1 < l2, the resulting phi is the orientation of the long side.
